one_liner: Attio CRM has a broad public REST API with OAuth 2.0 and API keys, free-plan access, webhooks, an OpenAPI spec, and an official hosted MCP server.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow (PKCE supported) for multi-workspace apps, registered at build.attio.com. Workspace API keys are sent as Bearer. HTTP Basic is also accepted, with the token as the username and a blank password.
access_notes: API access is included on every plan, including Free. No approval gate. Unpublished OAuth apps can be shared with other workspaces. Installing an app requires a workspace admin.
blocker_notes: No significant blocker. Rate limits are 100 reads/sec and 25 writes/sec.

evidence.quote: You should prefer the OAuth 2.0 flow if building an app for multiple workspaces. If you are building an app for a single workspace, you can manually generate an API key

We also support [HTTP Basic Authentication](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Authorization#basic_authentication), where the username is the token and the password is left blank
There is no separate developer signup, no approval gate, and no enterprise-only restriction.
The free plan is a real plan rather than a trial, and because API access is on it, you can build and test an integration end to end
an endpoint catalogue spanning custom objects, records, lists, notes, tasks, files, meetings, and call recordings.
an [OpenAPI spec](https://docs.attio.com/rest-api/endpoint-reference/openapi) is downloadable, and API access ships on every plan, including free.
Attio MCP is Attio's hosted MCP server that gives AI tools secure access to your Attio workspace.
